message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image.  
I’ll give you both the **`gcloud` CLI** command (the easiest way) and the **REST API** payload (in case you want to call the API directly from your own code).

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** and the **NVIDIA GPU Driver** package must be enabled in the project.  
> * You need the `gcloud` SDK installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * The target zone must support GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-b`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE",count="$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Gives the instance a 100 GB SSD boot disk. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` | Optional: runs a shell script on first boot (see below). |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for installing drivers). |

### Optional: Install NVIDIA drivers automatically

Create a file named `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
# Reboot so the driver loads
sudo reboot
```

Make it executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

When the instance starts, the script will run, install the driver, and reboot.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl)

If you prefer to call the API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), here’s a minimal `curl` example that sends a JSON payload to the Compute Engine API.

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# JSON payload
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# POST request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

### Notes on the REST payload

* `machineType` and `acceleratorType` are fully qualified URLs.  
* The `metadata` section can include a `startup-script` that runs on first boot (same as the CLI example).  
* The `accessToken` is obtained via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`.  
* You can also use a service account key file and exchange it for a token if you’re running this from a non‑interactive environment.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
# SSH into the instance
gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE"

# Inside the instance
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

### TL;DR

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=my-gcp-project \
  --zone=us-central1-b \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

That’s all you need to spin up a GPU‑enabled Ubuntu 20.04 instance on Google Cloud!
